criteria.note: The WARP-0603 TrackerAdapter seam (.warp/tracker_adapter.py) gains assign(obj_id, assignee) as a fifth explicit audited write beside comment/set_status/create_or_update_epic/create_or_update_child, with the SAME base-owned guarantees. The public assign() validates both inputs BY NAME through _require (a blank or None obj_id or assignee raises TrackerAdapterError before any surface call), FAILS LOUD on an object the tracker does not hold (raise TrackerItemNotFound via _has_object, never a silent no-op), then records the write in the base-owned audit (_record 'assign') and returns the subclass primitive's changed bool. FakeTracker._assign is idempotent by TARGET assignee (rec.assignee == assignee returns False, a real change returns True) and each record now carries an 'assignee' (added to _new_record and copied through seed_item). The live JiraCloudAdapter._assign and ConfluenceCloudAdapter._assign (.warp/tracker_intake.py) both RAISE by name (assignment against live Jira wired in WARP-1005; a wiki page has no assignee), so the live path is not exercised here. Selftest teeth confirm real-change True, repeat False, the write appears in writes() as op 'assign', a blank assignee raises TrackerAdapterError, and a missing object raises TrackerItemNotFound.

At the ready-to-test point the mirror (.warp/tracker_mirror.py) posts a KEYED comment (key '<sid>:artifacts', at most once under at-least-once replay) carrying only the links that EXIST. _artifact_links(evs) gathers commit/pr/proof from the lifecycle events with latest-non-empty-wins and returns None for any the events do not carry; the block appends 'commit ...', 'pull request ...', 'proof ...' only for the non-None values, so a commit-only build yields a comment with the commit and NEITHER an invented pull request NOR an invented proof. It writes only a comment through the audited seam, never a spec or plan definition. Selftest asserts the all-three case carries commit + PR + proof, the commit-only case contains 'beef5678' but not 'pull request' or 'proof' (no fabrication), a pre-ready-to-test point posts zero artifact comments, and a replay posts no duplicate (state byte-identical). _artifact_links reads only the event dict keys, never fabricating a link.

The reassign hangs off ONLY the ready-to-test transition, guarded by any(ev.type == READY_TO_TEST_EVENT), READY_TO_TEST_EVENT == 'verdict.recorded' (in_review). resolve_reviewer(config, repo_id, reporter) implements PLAN-0010 C7 precedence exactly: a per-repo 'reviewer' in .warp/trackers.json overrides a global 'reviewer', either falling back to the ticket's reporter (carried on spec metadata via build_spec_index fm.get('reporter'), read from the repo not the tracker), and returns None (assignee left UNTOUCHED, never invented) when none is known; a present reviewer that is not a non-empty string raises MirrorError by name. The reassign guard 'reviewer and reviewer != agent and adapter.assign(...)' never assigns TO the single Agent user and is idempotent by target. An earlier lifecycle point (spec.ready) never reaches the block so the fleet keeps the ticket. Selftest teeth: at ready-to-test the child goes to the reporter default exactly once; a pre-ready-to-test spec.ready replay leaves the Agent (reassignments 0); a per-repo reviewer overrides the reporter default (qa-lead); and the non-tautology pair proves causation.

Gate-tested over the FakeTracker offline with REAL, load-bearing teeth. TEETH PROVEN BY MUTATION: setting READY_TO_TEST_EVENT to an earlier lifecycle point ('spec.ready') turned the crux case RED - 'mirror does NOT reassign before ready-to-test (the fleet keeps the ticket on the Agent)' failed, along with the reassign-once and non-tautology cases, at 1430 passed / 3 failed; git checkout of .warp/tracker_mirror.py reverted it, git diff --quiet is clean, HEAD is still a57b2ba, and selftest is back to 1433 / 0. The WARP-1004 block asserts reassign-once and links-once at ready-to-test, no reassign and no links before it (non-tautological removal-then-add pair), idempotent byte-identical replay (state_digest unchanged), a per-repo reviewer override, a commit-only no-fabrication case, and assign to a missing object fails loud. No live network in the gate.

findings.text: Non-blocking, behavioral documentation. The ready-to-test handoff (reassign + artifact links) is gated on the PRESENCE of verdict.recorded anywhere in the deduped event stream, not on in_review being the child's latest mapped status. A single fresh mirror pass over an already-terminal stream (verdict.recorded followed by spec.shipped) therefore performs both the terminal status transition and the handoff in one pass. This is correct and idempotent (a build that recorded a verdict did enter review, the reassign is by-target and the comment is keyed, matching the AC4 replay teeth), so it is correctness-preserving, not a defect. Worth noting only so an operator knows the handoff is presence-triggered rather than latest-status-triggered.

summary: WARP-1004 (outbound reassignment and artifact links, W4 of PLAN-0010) passes with notes at a57b2ba, zero blocking findings. The ASSIGN SEAM OP (AC1) is fail-loud and correct: assign() validates both inputs by name (TrackerAdapterError on blank/None), raises TrackerItemNotFound on an object the tracker does not hold (never a silent no-op), records the write in the base-owned audit, and is idempotent by TARGET assignee (real change True, repeat False); the live JiraCloud and Confluence _assign both RAISE for the later increment (WARP-1005), so only the FakeTracker path runs. The REASSIGN TIMING (AC3, the crux) is right and its teeth are load-bearing: the handoff hangs off ONLY verdict.recorded (in_review), reassigns from the single Agent to resolve_reviewer (per-repo reviewer over global reviewer over the ticket reporter, C7), guarded so it never assigns to the Agent and never invents an assignee, and is idempotent by target. Proven non-tautological by mutation: moving READY_TO_TEST_EVENT to an earlier point (spec.ready) turned the 'does NOT reassign before ready-to-test' case RED (1430/3), and git checkout restored a clean tree (git diff --quiet clean, HEAD unchanged at a57b2ba) and 1433/0. ARTIFACT LINKS (AC2) post a keyed comment at most once and never fabricate: commit always, PR and proof only when the events carry them (commit-only stays commit-only). ONE-WAY (NG5) holds: the mirror writes only comments, assignment, and status through the audited seam, never a spec or plan definition, and the reporter fallback comes from spec front-matter, not by reading the tracker back, so the repository stays the single source of truth. NON-LLM: pure stdlib control logic over the injected seam, no subprocess/network/agent call. ENGINE SYNC (AC5) is honest: two scope:repo-only capability entries in their homes, capabilities.yaml byte-identical across all eight copies, template-sync and pack-drift green (7 packs), the full gate GREEN at R (verify.sh 5 run / 18 na / 0 waived / 0 undeclared, selftest 1433/0), no protected path touched, RULE #1 clean in the additions. manifest.json binds to R with plan_hash sha256:f6a5cc8e425f566b (matching plan.py hash PLAN-0010) and a proof_digest that recomputes to sha256:85fb7e7bbaf5ddea. One non-blocking note: the handoff is gated on the presence of verdict.recorded in the stream rather than on in_review being the latest status, which is idempotent and correctness-preserving. Verdict: pass_with_notes.
